survey: The object is a cartoon headstone, seen in three-quarter view from the front left. It has two parts. The upright slab has a rounded top and a raised cross carved near the top. A crack runs down from a chipped top-right corner to about mid-height. The slab sits flat and centred on a wider rectangular base. The base rests on a stone ledge and casts a contact shadow, so it is grounded. Two blobs of moss cling to the top-left corner of the slab, wrapping over its edge, and a larger moss patch sits on the base against the slab's lower-left corner. A small orange flower with a green stem lies flat on the right side of the base. Every part touches a surface: nothing floats and nothing passes through anything else. The partial crack makes sense: it opens wider at the top, where the corner broke away, and narrows to nothing lower down, so the stone still holds together.

errors.where: Broken top-right corner of the slab, where the crack starts
errors.what: The broken edge is cut into three neat, flat, evenly spaced steps, like stairs or a stack of layers. Solid stone does not break into regular terraces, so on a close look the break reads as built rather than broken.

fix: Make the chipped top-right corner of the headstone an irregular, jagged break in solid stone, with an uneven rough edge and no flat stepped ledges, joining naturally into the crack below.
